name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
description: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) is a benchmark for text embeddings spanning 8 embedding tasks covering a total of 58 datasets and 112 languages. It unifies datasets from different embedding tasks into a common, accessible evaluation framework and comes with open-source code and a public leaderboard.
creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers
citeAs: Muennighoff, Niklas; Tazi, Nouamane; Magne, Loïc; Reimers, Nils. MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. arXiv:2210.07316v3, 2023.
rai:dataCollection: MTEB unifies 58 datasets from 8 embedding tasks: bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, STS and summarization. It incorporates existing benchmarks such as SemEval datasets (STS11 - STS22) and BEIR, and also includes custom-made datasets for MTEB. The benchmark is extensible via a single file that specifies the task and a Hugging Face dataset name where the data has been uploaded. Custom clustering datasets were created using public APIs from arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv, and additional datasets were created for MTEB using available data from Reddit and StackExchange posts.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web API, Software Collection, Others
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The benchmark reuses datasets from SemEval, BEIR, BUCC, Tatoeba, Kaggle competitions, Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, arXiv, bioRxiv/medRxiv APIs, and other publicly available datasets. For custom clustering datasets, source texts are paper titles and abstracts from arXiv, bioRxiv, and medRxiv. RedditClusteringP2P uses available Reddit post data, and StackExchangeClusteringP2P uses available StackExchange post data.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Several clustering tasks are framed as both sentence-to-sentence and paragraph-to-paragraph tasks. For S2S datasets, the input text is simply the title of the paper, while for P2P the input text is the concatenation of the title and the abstract. For arXiv multiple categories can be given to a single paper so only the first one is used. For every clustering dataset, split and strategy, subsets of labels are selected and articles are sampled from those labels, yielding splits with varying amounts and sizes of clusters.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: MTEB groups datasets into sentence-to-sentence (S2S), paragraph-to-paragraph (P2P), and sentence-to-paragraph (S2P) categories. MTEB imposes no limit on input length, leaving it up to models to truncate if necessary. For P2P clustering tasks such as ArxivClustering, abstracts are concatenated to titles. Evaluation uses predefined train, dev, and test splits from source datasets; the authors evaluate on test splits of all datasets except MSMARCO, where the dev split is used following prior work.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are inherited from the underlying datasets and vary by task. Examples include human-written labels for classification tasks, duplicate/paraphrase labels for pair classification and reranking, relevance judgments for retrieval, continuous similarity scores for STS, and human assessments of machine-generated summaries for summarization. For custom clustering datasets, cluster labels are generated using categories given to papers by humans. In bitext mining datasets, annotated pairs correspond to translated sentence pairs.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For pair classification, distances are computed with various metrics and the best binary threshold is used to compute metrics. For STS and summarization, multiple distance metrics are benchmarked against ground truth similarities or human assessments, with cosine-similarity-based Spearman correlation used as the main metric. The paper notes that controlling for data contamination between benchmark datasets and model training datasets is challenging and that overlap is ignored in MTEB scores.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: MTEB software is available open-source, with datasets and a leaderboard on the Hugging Face Hub. The benchmark is intended to continue development through community pull requests for datasets, tasks, or metrics. The authors aim for reproducibility through versioning at a dataset and software level, and JSON files corresponding to all results in the paper are made available together with the benchmark.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark includes multilingual data covering 112 languages. Some included datasets contain human-related content such as customer reviews, online banking queries, Twitter messages, movie reviews, Alexa utterances, comments from the Civil Comments platform, Reddit posts, StackExchange posts, and news or forum text. Explicit sensitive attributes collected are not described in the paper.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to provide reliable embedding performance estimates and make selecting the right embedding model easier for future research or industry applications of text embeddings. The paper notes that blind application of embedding models to new use cases in industry can occur without proper evaluation, and MTEB is intended to simplify future embedding research and model selection.
rai:dataBiases: MTEB average scores are biased towards tasks with many datasets, notably retrieval, classification and clustering, because tasks have different numbers of datasets and summarization consists of only a single dataset. The paper also notes possible data contamination, for example parts of SciDocsRR likely being included in some models' training data, and states that controlling for overlap of MTEB datasets with model training datasets is challenging. Multilingual coverage is uneven because retrieval and clustering are English-only.
rai:dataLimitations: The paper lists several limitations: very long document datasets are missing; tasks are imbalanced in number of datasets, biasing average scores toward retrieval, classification and clustering; multilinguality is incomplete because retrieval and clustering are English-only and there are no code datasets; and the benchmark focuses solely on natural language applications and not additional modalities such as image content. The authors also note that overlap between benchmark datasets and model training datasets is ignored because controlling for contamination is challenging.
rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is designed for evaluation and benchmarking of text embedding models across 8 tasks and 58 datasets, including multilingual evaluation. It is used to evaluate models on predefined train/dev/test splits depending on task, with test splits used for most datasets and the MSMARCO dev split used following prior work. It supports benchmarking any embedding model through an API and provides a public leaderboard and JSON results for reproducible comparison.
